hero_title: An AI interviewer that won't go easy on you.
hero_lead: You upload your resume. Rally reads it, then runs a live interview — same questions, same pressure, same follow-ups as a real senior engineer. It doesn't quiz you on facts. It tears apart everything vague until "I worked on it" has real numbers behind it.
hero_cta_note: No credit card required · New users only
hero_eyebrow: Covers FAANG · Google · Microsoft · Meta · Amazon · ByteDance · Tencent · Alibaba · DoorDash · Stripe
hero_signature: Rally · Won't agree with you just to be nice
hero_evidence_heading: How it differs from general AI
selling_point_1_desc: You say "I worked on performance." It asks three follow-ups — which metric, what's the baseline, what code did you change. If it can't stand, it switches angles.
selling_point_1_sample_quote: You say: "I helped optimize the rec system"
selling_point_1_sample_reply: Hold on — which metric? What's the baseline?
selling_point_2_title: It trains on last month's real questions
selling_point_2_desc: Not LRU again. The question asked in a real interview last month — Flink exactly-once, Kafka rebalance offset drift, the fresh stuff.
selling_point_2_sample_reply: How does Flink state recovery guarantee exactly-once?
selling_point_3_title: It scores by pinning to a specific sentence
selling_point_3_desc: No single opaque 7/10. Every deduction and bonus is annotated on the exact sentence you said — so you know which line to fix next time.
selling_point_3_sample_reply: −2: no unit, no baseline, no time window.
selling_point_4_title: It talks like a real interviewer, not a chatbot
selling_point_4_desc: No "Great question! Let me explain…" energy. It pauses, sighs, pushes back, and pulls you back when you ramble — pacing, follow-ups, tone, all modeled on real interviewers.
selling_point_4_sample_reply: …that's not related to Redis. Back to it — why zset, not list?
selling_points_label: How it differs from general AI

updates_logic_headline: Pulls you back within 5 seconds of going off-topic
updates_logic_note: Pulls you back within 5 seconds of going off-topic. A vague "I worked on it" gets chased for 5 rounds until you have the numbers, baseline, and time window to back it up.
